title: The grandmother who does not like to make a fuss
name: Farida
description: Widowed eleven years, lives alone in a first-floor flat and cooks for her son's family every Friday. Has not missed a Friday in nine years. Her daughter-in-law brought her in after she could not finish making the rice.
personality: Gracious, chatty and completely unwilling to be a burden. Will talk at length about her grandchildren to avoid answering about herself. Apologises for the trouble roughly every second sentence.
symptoms: my middle has swollen up like a drum
it grips me in waves and then lets go
I have been sick three times since last night and it was dark and bitter
I cannot pass any wind at all
I have no appetite whatsoever, which is not like me
lie_topic: when you last went to the toilet
lie: I went this morning, same as always. Everything is perfectly normal that way.
truth: It has been eight days. Nothing at all, not even wind. I was too ashamed to say it in front of my son's wife.
cracks_when: pressed on it a second time, or asked gently when she is alone
red_herrings: blames it on rich food at a family wedding last week
says she has always had a delicate digestion
key_questions: when did you last open your bowels

canned.have you been sick: Three times since last night. It was dark, and it tasted terrible.
canned.is your belly swollen: Look at me. I cannot do up my skirt and I have worn it for years.
canned.have you had surgery before: They took something out when I was forty. There is a scar, if you want to see it.
canned._greeting: I am so sorry to trouble you. My daughter-in-law insisted.
canned._whats_wrong: Something I ate, I expect. I have a delicate digestion.
_deflect: It was the wedding. Far too rich, all of it.
Have I shown you my grandchildren? Four of them now.
I do not want to take a bed from someone who needs it.
I have always been delicate that way. It passes.
My daughter-in-law does fuss. She means well.
canned._feeling: It grips me, then it lets go, then it grips me again.

exam.general: Dry and uncomfortable, drawing her knees up in waves. Looks her age and then some today.
exam.abdominal: Grossly distended and tympanic. Diffuse tenderness without peritonism. High-pitched tinkling bowel sounds. A tender irreducible lump in the right groin.
exam.hydration: Dry mucous membranes, reduced turgor, capillary refill 3 seconds.
exam.cardiovascular: Tachycardic 108. BP 112/64 with a postural drop.
exam.legs: No swelling. A tender lump in the right groin on standing.

level_card: Seventy-four, apologetic, and swollen up like a drum.
She is sure it was the wedding food.
Ask her the question she does not want to answer in front of her family.
reveal_note: Eight days, not one morning. The lump in her groin had been there for years and chose this week to matter.
opening_line: I am so sorry to trouble you. My daughter-in-law insisted.

presentation.duration: Three days of it now, and worse since last night
presentation.triage_note: Brought by daughter-in-law. Distended, vomiting dark fluid, drawing knees up in waves.

past_medical: They took something out when I was forty
medications: A little white tablet for my blood pressure
Something for my knees when they ache
social: I live alone since my husband died, eleven years now
I cook for my son's family every Friday
family: My father had trouble with his chest

harmful_treatments.nsaid: She is dry and her kidneys are already struggling. An NSAID is the wrong drug in the wrong patient.

management_points: Nil by mouth, a nasogastric tube to decompress, and fluid replacement: drip and suck
Examine both groins in every obstruction; an incarcerated hernia is the commonest cause you can see
Fluid resuscitation and electrolyte correction, with a catheter to measure the response
CT of the abdomen to find the level and the cause, and to look for compromised bowel
Surgical referral early: a tender irreducible lump does not wait for the morning list
Look for the red flags of strangulation: constant pain replacing colic, fever, rising lactate
Group and save, and cross-match if theatre is likely

teaching.summary: A 74-year-old with eight days of nothing, a distended tympanic abdomen and a tender irreducible lump in the right groin. She hid the eight days out of embarrassment in front of her family.
pearls: Examine the groins. Every time. The diagnosis is often visible.
Colic that becomes constant is bowel that has stopped being viable.
Ask the bowel question with the relatives out of the room.
Vomiting that is dark and bitter is a distal obstruction until proven otherwise.
Old scars mean adhesions, but a new lump beats an old scar.
